test_title: RRB Group D Previous Year Paper (Held on: 25 Aug 2022 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: The Right to Education in the Indian Constitution was added by introducing a new Article, ________, in the Chapter on Fundamental Rights in 2002 by the 86th Constitutional Amendment.
solution:
The correct answer is __**21A**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **21A** was added to the Indian Constitution by the 86th Constitutional Amendment in 2002.
 
• This amendment made the Right to Education a fundamental right for children aged 6 to 14 years.
 
• Article 21A states that "The State shall provide free and compulsory education to all children of the age of six to fourteen years in such manner as the State may, by law, determine."
 
• This was a significant step towards ensuring educational opportunities for all children in India.
 
• The amendment is part of the broader effort to improve literacy rates and educational standards in the country.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The 86th Amendment also introduced Article 51A(k) which made it a fundamental duty of parents to provide opportunities for education to their children aged 6 to 14 years.
 
• Prior to this amendment, the Directive Principles of State Policy under Article 45 urged the state to provide free and compulsory education, but it was not enforceable by law.
 
• The Right to Education Act (RTE) 2009 was enacted to operationalize the provisions of Article 21A.
 
• The RTE Act lays down the norms and standards for schools, pupil-teacher ratios, and infrastructure, ensuring quality education for all children.
 
• This landmark amendment and subsequent legislation have been pivotal in advancing educational rights and access in India.
